subject: Clarification: SOC 2 evidence & responsibility mapping for cloud subservice
messages:
From: Northbridge Audit Services <audit@northbridge-audit.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2: Clarify cloud subservice coverage and evidence requested

Hi Grace,

We're starting Northbridge's walkthrough for your SOC 2 Type II review. The control owner for our engagement asked us to confirm whether Redwood treats your cloud provider (AWS) as a subservice organization with a carve-out, or if AWS responsibilities are documented as shared controls in your responsibility mapping. Specifically we need clarity on: 

- Whether you consider AWS in-scope via a bridge letter or via reliance on AWS' SOC report (carve-out).
- Which controls are considered solely managed by AWS (e.g., physical security, certain hypervisor controls) versus those Redwood owns (e.g., application-level access, key management if applicable).
- Evidence: request for the latest Redwood SOC 2 Type II report covering the period ending 2026-06-01, and the AWS SOC report(s) you relied on. If you use customer-managed KMS or a BYOK model, please indicate and provide supporting docs.

We'd like to receive the clarifications and any supporting documents by next Tuesday, 24 Nov, so we can schedule the control testing window. If you plan to provide a bridge letter instead of full carve-out documentation, please note the effective audit period the bridge covers.

Thanks,
Amanda Jenkins
Senior Manager, Northbridge Audit Services
---
Attachments requested: SOC 2 Type II (Redwood), AWS SOC report(s), responsibility mapping (matrix)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Amanda Jenkins <audit@northbridge-audit.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2: Clarify cloud subservice coverage and evidence requested

Amanda,

Thanks for the note — happy to clarify. Short answers up front: Redwood treats AWS as a subservice organization and we rely on AWS SOC reports for infrastructure controls; we do not carve those controls back in. For controls around customer data encryption keys we have two patterns depending on the customer deployment: Hosted/Dedicated (Redwood KMS with envelope encryption) vs Private (customer-managed KMS/BYOK).

Next steps I propose:
- I'll attach our most recent SOC 2 Type II (covers 2025-06-01 to 2026-06-01).
- Diego will attach the AWS SOC report references we used and a short responsibility matrix.
- Can you confirm whether Northbridge needs a signed bridge letter? We typically provide a standard bridge letter when customers request one to cover gaps between AWS and our audit period.

High-level ownership mapping (summary):
- AWS: physical data center, hypervisor, networking fabric, host OS (AWS SOC), underlying region DR controls.
- Redwood: application-level access controls, tenant isolation, encryption-at-rest keys (unless customer-managed), logging/monitoring in our stack, patching at the application layer.

Cc'ing Diego and Evelyn for the attachments and any additional context.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_20250601-20260601.pdf (stub)
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Amanda Jenkins <audit@northbridge-audit.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2: Clarify cloud subservice coverage and evidence requested

Amanda — attaching the artifacts we referenced:

- aws-soc-report-2025.pdf (pointer to AWS public SOC 2 report we relied on)
- redwood_cloud_responsibility_matrix_20261122.xlsx (a control-by-control mapping showing service owner = AWS or Redwood)

A few notes from the matrix:
1) Where we list "AWS" as owner, that refers to infrastructure controls (data center physical security, network segregation at host level, hypervisor). Those are not carved into Redwood's scope.
2) For encryption: Hosted/Dedicated customers can opt for Redwood-managed keys (Redwood KMS) — in that case Redwood owns KMS envelope key rotation and access controls; customers using our Private deployment (VPC/On‑prem) often bring their own KMS keys (BYOK) and then the customer is responsible for key material. The matrix flags each control by deployment type.
3) We maintain application logs and SIEM alerts; we ingest cloud provider audit logs but do not rely only on provider logs for control evidence.

Let us know if you need a template bridge letter. If a bridge letter is required, Grace, do we want legal to sign or should the Head of Compliance sign a standard one?

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Compliance Operations
---
Attachments: aws-soc-report-2025.pdf (stub), redwood_cloud_responsibility_matrix_20261122.xlsx (stub)
From: Amanda Jenkins <audit@northbridge-audit.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2: Clarify cloud subservice coverage and evidence requested

Thanks Grace and Diego — that was helpful. A couple follow ups before we finalize our test plan: 

1) Please confirm the exact audit period covered by the AWS SOC report you provided (we saw 2024 calendar year on the AWS doc; need to confirm overlap with Redwood's period).
2) We will accept the responsibility matrix. For our report we also need either: (a) a bridge letter that explicitly references the AWS SOC period and states Redwood's reliance, or (b) an attestation that the AWS SOC controls were sustained through your audit period (2025-06-01 to 2026-06-01).

If you can provide a drafted bridge letter, we can review and route for signature. Otherwise an email attestation signed by your compliance lead is acceptable. 

Would you be able to turn that around by end of day Wednesday (24 Nov)? That will keep us on schedule for control testing the week of 29 Nov.

Best,
Amanda
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Amanda Jenkins <audit@northbridge-audit.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2: Clarify cloud subservice coverage and evidence requested

Amanda — quick update: 

- Confirmed: AWS SOC report covers calendar year 2025 (we use the most recent public report); we have included it for transparency. We are providing a short bridge letter that ties Redwood's audited period (2025-06-01 to 2026-06-01) to the AWS report and clarifies which controls are outside Redwood's scope.
- Attached: redwood_cloud_responsibility_matrix_20261122.xlsx and a draft bridge letter (we provided the DocuSign link for signature once you confirm language).

Neha (copied) will route the bridge letter for signature — Neha, we typically have the Head of Compliance sign; please advise if Legal should sign as well.

If that works, you should have the signed bridge letter by EOD Wednesday. 

Thanks,
Grace

---
